text:
alex: thinking out loud — I'm trying to make a synthetic traffic generator that reliably surfaces perf regressions that only show up in long-tail + microburst combos. current flakiness is killing our bisects. ideas?

maria: +1 on flakiness. primary suspects: kernel selection path nondeterminism, batching heuristics reacting to slightly different arrival order, and KV cache warmup variance.

kyle: we saw this before — different kernel chosen when the observed seq_len distribution skews for a few seconds. need to force identical seq_len and tokenization distribution across runs.

alex: yep. plan sketch: 1) deterministic RNG seeds, 2) replay mode that replays recorded arrival timestamps (optionally scaled), 3) explicit warmup phase to pre-populate KV cache then pause before test. thoughts?

jin: sounds good. small nit: pre-populating KV cache needs to mimic realistic prefix keys, not just repeated single prompt. otherwise kernel behaves differently (prefill vs incremental kv growth).

olivia: also add a "jittered Poisson" mode — mean QPS + configurable jitter amplitude — that lets us inject microbursts while keeping overall rate stable. saves churn compared to pure spike tests.

alex: agreed. here's a config draft — please critique:

```
mode: replay  # replay | poisson | mmpp | fixed
seed: 420
replay_scale: 1.0
sequence_length_dist: "empirical://path/to/hist.pb"
warmup_phase:
  duration_s: 30
  num_unique_prefixes: 500
burst_profile:
  type: mmpp
  high_rate: 1200
  low_rate: 50
  high_duration_ms: [50,200]
  low_duration_ms: [1000,5000]
```

maria: a few suggestions: add per-shard affinity control so we can pin traffic to a specific GPU shard; include tokenized size distribution in the log header so run-to-run comparisons are apples-to-apples; and capture kernel selection trace (kernel_id, seq_len, timestamp) at debug level.

kyle: for apples-to-apples, also ensure we capture the runtime kernel selection inputs: hardware flags (SM version), cudnn/driver versions, and any quantization knobs. put those into the test artifact metadata.

jen (ci-bot): note: CI load runner currently does not support replay scaling >2.0 without causing scheduling issues. filing ticket #INF-1224.

alex: thanks — incremental checklist: deterministic seed, replay mode, warmup prefill with realistic prefixes, per-shard pinning, kernel selection trace, hardware/driver metadata. want to add a "kv-consistency" test where we intentionally vary warmup size to see when kernel choice flips.

jin: +1 on kv-consistency test. record kv hit rate timeline and batch size distribution. kernel selection flips often coincide with sustained batch_size>1 for ~200ms windows.

olivia: can we add an automatic regression detector? e.g., run baseline and new build 5 times each, compare 95/99/99.9 latency windows and batch histograms with KS-test and flag >X% divergence.

kyle: yes, and store the failing run's replay file so we can reproduce locally (seed + arrival timestamps + token seqs).

alex: implementation note: generator should output a compact artifact per run: metadata.json, arrivals.bin (int64 microseconds), tokens.bin (packed tokens), header with seed+seq_dist_hash. makes debugging easier.

maria: don't forget to add a mode that randomly flips kernel-selection-related flags (quantization levels, use_fp16_kernels) to stress the selection logic in CI. randomized fuzzing catches a lot.

alex: final question — what about duration? short runs (<2m) miss long-tail. long runs are expensive. compromise?

jin: run a 2m canonical test in PRs for fast feedback; schedule periodic nightlies that run 30m to collect long-tail. if PR shows small regression, run the long-nightly replay to get coverage.

olivia: also run a "burst-sensitivity" sweep: keep average QPS fixed, vary burst amplitude and duty cycle to map where regressions manifest. that gives a 2D sensitivity surface we can use to pick representative stress points.

alex: perfect. I'll draft a PR with the generator plus the artifact format and a small harness that can replay an artifact exactly. linking when ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/XXXX

kyle: tiny: include a `--dry-run-checks` mode that validates seed+replay determinism (replay twice, assert identical arrivals). saved us last time.

alex: will do. thanks everyone, this is actionable. I'll post the PR and a short how-to for reproducing kernel-selection flips locally. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: created issue INF-1224 for CI scaling limits (assigned to eng-infra).
